_meta.description: The twelve connections Dossiq has to systems outside it, seeded for the Integrations page (pluggable-integration-registry). The status a row carries is the status the app can back on a fresh instance: nine are unconfigured because nothing has been saved or probed yet, and KvK is unavailable because nothing calls its adapter. BRP and KvK were both seeded `unavailable` with the message "Specified, not built yet", and that was false for both. Each ships two adapter tiers (a dormant Log adapter and a real HTTP one), a DI registrar bound from ExternalRegisterRegistrar, and unit tests. BRP is `unconfigured` because it IS built and IS called, by ConflictOfInterestService for the belangenconflict check, and reaches nothing until `integration.brp.mode` moves off its `log` default. KvK stays `unavailable` for a different reason than the one it claimed: the adapter is built and bound, and no service or screen injects KvkHandelsregisterAdapterInterface, so setting its mode changes nothing. InitiatorPicker.vue calls neither: it searches the seeded brpPerson and kvkCompany register sets through the object store. NO ROW IS SEEDED configured — only a save or a probe may write that, which is what makes the page worth reading. The order follows row A34 of the round-2 placement matrix. settingsUrl points at the anchor its section carries in AdminRoot.vue. THREE rows carry none: BRP and KvK because no admin section writes their mode key, and PDOK because it has no admin section at all — its pdok_* app-config keys are read by the map components and written by nothing an admin can open. The change's design counted eight anchors; AdminRoot.vue has seven sections to anchor, and inventing a link into a section that does not exist is the one thing this page is here to stop. TWO ROWS ARE SEEDED `simulated`, and that is a claim the app CAN back on a fresh instance: Berichtenbox and the beschikking template engine both resolve to a mock adapter unless an integrator names a real one in the `berichtenbox_adapter` or `beschikking_template_adapter` app-config key, so `simulated` is what is true before anybody configures anything. Saving a real adapter class flips the row to `configured`; clearing it flips the row back. Neither row carries a settingsUrl, for the same reason PDOK does not: no admin section writes those keys yet, and inventing a link into a section that does not exist is the one thing this page is here to stop. The row's own message names the key instead, so an integrator can set it with `occ config:app:set`. Neither ships a transport, and neither should: both are per-customer contracts and belong in integriq.
